lede: Bacari is a Venetian-inspired small plates restaurant with Mediterranean-influenced dishes by Chef Lior Hillel. Owned by brothers Danny and Robert Kronfli, the group has opened ten restaurants across Los Angeles and San Diego since starting in West Adams in 2008, has two more under construction, and is now expanding to Texas. Our in-house team leads all the creative. We're looking for a licensed Austin architect of record to be our technical partner: code strategy, construction documents, permitting and engineers, and our eyes on site through construction.
site: Lease is in final negotiation. We're using the diligence period now; our clock starts when we sign.
A two-level Craftsman bungalow of about 3,500 sf, with roughly 5,000 sf of decks, patio and lot.
**Street level:** the former hot line kitchen, an interior bar, a small dining room, two restrooms and a wraparound deck.
**Parking-lot level:** prep and storage, a speakeasy, and the existing patio and outdoor dining under large oak trees.
A kitchen fire destroyed the upper roof and damaged the upper floor. The landlord has already demolished the burned roof; the foundation is sound.
The large tree out front is a heritage tree, and there may be one or two protected trees around the edge of the lot.
We don't yet know whether the building has fire sprinklers, and we don't have a property survey.
**Structural report:** [forensic structural evaluation](https://drive.google.com/file/d/1a_F9nrt6AYNLMr4hueXev_6UG8kQtx2r/view) by Haag Engineering, June 23, 2026 (PDF).

**Site documents:** drawings and other documents from the broker are in [this Dropbox folder](https://www.dropbox.com/scl/fo/l78yw52u3vvptshoroxcz/ANGuSrRnEJv6FhUS32XAR-A?rlkey=emji5et80mk7x1hixnby8ciks&dl=0).
build: **Parking-lot level:** the entire kitchen (hot line, pass, prep and storage) plus guest restrooms. Food runs up the stairs; no dumbwaiter.
**Street level:** remove the old kitchen and turn the whole floor into a much larger bar and dining room, with restrooms.
**Backyard:** roughly double the lot-level patio and seating into a garden-style backyard with its own outdoor bar, so drinks never travel the stairs.
**Parking:** keep the back ~30% of the lot for parking, screened from guests.
**Decks:** extend the existing decks and possibly add one near street level. Cover guests wherever code and structure allow, and keep the trees as a feature.
**Style:** Craftsman, leaning into the bungalow inside, outside and in the landscaping. Our team designs it; you help us build it to detail.
New kitchen, new bars and all-new finishes throughout.
The outdoor layout and flow is where we'll lean on you most for code and structure.
feel: Each location has its own personality, but they share a backyard warmth: bars that open to the patio, mature trees and string lights outside; wood beams, white plaster, vintage art, warm lighting and checkered tile inside. Every Bacari takes its style from its building, like Art Deco in Beverly Hills, New Orleans in North Park and Spanish in Sherman Oaks. In Austin it will be Craftsman.
services: Existing conditions: a field survey with topography, as-built drawings of what survived the fire, and any existing plans the city has on file.
Code strategy up front: occupancy, fire sprinklers, the site plan exemption and the new-construction thresholds, with a clear read on what each design choice triggers.
Design support: turn our team's design into a code-compliant layout for both levels, the decks and the backyard, with options and a cost check where it matters.
Accessibility and exiting: Texas Accessibility Standards compliance (TDLR registration, RAS review and inspection), plus occupant loads and exiting for the decks and outdoor seating.
Construction documents: a complete, stamped drawing set and specifications a contractor can build from.
Full permit set to the City of Austin, building and health, with the site plan exemption run alongside the building permit.
Structural, MEP and civil engineering, including a new fire line tap if we need sprinklers. We prefer one contract with you as the single point of contact.
Site and tree review with the City of Austin for the heritage tree and work near the oaks, coordinating with an arborist.
Health code layout (hand, three-compartment and floor sinks, drains). Chef Lior specs the kitchen from our standard equipment book, so no kitchen consultant is needed.
Technical drawings of our bar and millwork designs, plus lighting and reflected ceiling plans. Finishes can follow during the build.
A Matterport scan of existing conditions, and 3D views tied to the plans where they help us review layouts.
Contractor referrals: Austin general contractors who like working cost-plus.
Construction administration: site visits as often as the build needs, answering contractor questions and keeping the design true to spec while we're in LA.
Close-out: punch list, record drawings and sign-off for the certificate of occupancy.
how: Our in-house team leads the creative: Robert and Maha on design, Darryl on construction and budgets, and Chef Lior on the kitchen. We want a technical partner and collaborator, not a firm that runs design end to end.
Each Bacari takes its look from its building, so details and finishes get decided as we build. The permit set covers structure, walls, layout and MEP.
Layout, structural and MEP changes get locked before construction starts.
We run jobs cost-plus with a general contractor who likes working that way, not fixed bids with change orders and credits.
Robert walks the site in late November. After that we're mostly in LA, a three-hour flight away, so you're our eyes on site.
Our goal is plans ready to submit as soon as the lease is signed.
Our past openings were remodels of existing restaurants, so this is our first major rebuild. We have kitchen plans to share, but no prior full plan sets.

**Permitting goals:** stay in the site plan exemption track rather than full site plan review (as we understand it, about 3,000 sf of scope and under 1,000 sf of new impervious cover), and stay below the thresholds that turn a repair into a new build, such as the 50%-of-valuation rule.
**Phasing:** permit the core work first, then add decks and covers in later permits as we grow into the backyard.
**Open questions:** whether sprinklers are unavoidable once we cover the decks and add seats, and whether moving the kitchen downstairs could trigger new-build status.
ask: Restaurant and bar projects you've completed in Austin, ideally with commercial kitchens or fire restoration, and any where you were the local architect for an owner-led design team.
Confirmation that you're a licensed Texas architect who can stamp the drawings.
How you'd approach sprinklers, the site plan exemption and the new-construction thresholds on this site.
An all-in fee from start to finish, with architecture, structural, MEP, civil, expediting and construction administration broken out, plus your estimate of city review and permit fees.
Your timeline from kickoff to permit submission, assuming we want to submit right after signing the lease.
Who would be on site during construction, and how often.
General contractors you'd recommend who work cost-plus.
